definitions.explanation: The wavering visual distortion caused by heated air rising from the ground on hot days.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}の{道|みち}に{陽炎|かげろう}が{立|た}つ。
examples.english: Heat shimmer rises from the summer road.

examples.japanese: {陽炎|かげろう}で{遠|とお}くの{景色|けしき}が{揺|ゆ}れて{見|み}える。
examples.english: The distant scenery appears to waver due to the heat haze.

examples.japanese: {真夏|まなつ}の{昼下|ひるさ}がり、アスファルトの{上|うえ}に{陽炎|かげろう}が{揺|ゆ}らめいていた。
examples.english: In the midsummer afternoon, heat haze was shimmering above the asphalt.

notes:
{陽炎|かげろう} is the wavering visual distortion caused by heated air rising from the ground on hot days. The kanji combine {陽|よう} (sun) and {炎|ほのお} (flame), reflecting the fiery shimmer visible above hot surfaces.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {陽炎|かげろう}が{立|た}つ: heat haze rises
- {陽炎|かげろう}が{揺|ゆ}らめく: heat haze shimmers
- {陽炎|かげろう}のように: like a mirage (fleeting, illusory)

SEASONAL REFERENCE:
A traditional spring {季語|きご} (seasonal word) in haiku, though it is most commonly observed on hot summer days.

LITERARY USE:
The dreamlike, ephemeral quality of {陽炎|かげろう} makes it a common literary metaphor for things that are fleeting or illusory. The classic Heian-era diary {蜻蛉日記|かげろうにっき} uses this imagery in its title.
